territorial_scope.description: Applies to covered providers of generative AI systems that are publicly accessible within the geographic boundaries of California.

evidence.quote: is publicly accessible within the geographic boundaries of the state

summary.short: California statute, operative 1 January 2026, requiring covered providers of publicly accessible generative AI systems with over 1,000,000 monthly visitors or users to offer a no-cost AI detection tool and to include latent disclosures in AI-generated image, video or audio content, with civil penalties of $5,000 per violation.
summary.long: Adds the California AI Transparency Act (Business and Professions Code Chapter 25). Covered providers, meaning persons producing generative AI systems with over 1,000,000 monthly visitors or users publicly accessible in California, must offer a free AI detection tool that outputs system provenance data but not personal provenance data, and collect feedback on its efficacy. Tool users' personal information and submitted content face collection and retention limits. They must offer users an optional manifest disclosure of AI-generated content and include latent disclosures (provider name, system name and version, creation time and date, unique identifier) in AI-generated image, video or audio content, detectable by the tool. Licenses must require maintenance of that capability; providers must revoke a license within 96 hours of learning a licensee removed it, and licensees must then stop using the system. Violations carry a $5,000 civil penalty per violation, recoverable in civil actions by the Attorney General, a city attorney or a county counsel; each day is a discrete violation and prevailing plaintiffs recover fees. Licensees failing to cease use may be sued for injunctive relief and fees. Exempt: services offering exclusively non-user-generated video game, television, streaming, movie or interactive experiences. Operative 1 January 2026.

thresholds.variable_text: monthly visitors or users of a generative AI system
thresholds.measurement: Monthly visitors or users of the provider's generative AI system; the text does not specify the counting window or who measures it
thresholds.consequence: A person that creates, codes or produces such a system becomes a covered provider subject to the chapter
thresholds.conditions: The system is publicly accessible within the geographic boundaries of the state

evidence.quote: has over 1,000,000 monthly visitors or users and is publicly accessible within the geographic boundaries of the state
“Artificial intelligence” or “AI” means an engineered or machine-based system that varies in its level of autonomy

“Covered provider” means a person that creates, codes, or otherwise produces a generative artificial intelligence system that has over 1,000,000 monthly visitors or users and is publicly accessible within the geographic boundaries of the state.
“Generative artificial intelligence system” or “GenAI system” means an artificial intelligence that can generate derived synthetic content, including text, images, video, and audio
“Latent” means present but not manifest.
“Manifest” means easily perceived, understood, or recognized by a natural person.

definitions.defined_in: Civil Code Sec. 1798.140 (by reference in Business and Professions Code Sec. 22757.1(g))

evidence.quote: “Personal information” has the same meaning as defined in Section 1798.140 of the Civil Code.

obligations.summary: Make available a free AI detection tool to users that assesses image, video or audio content for the provider's GenAI system, outputs system provenance data but not personal provenance data, is publicly accessible (reasonable access limits allowed), accepts uploads or URLs, and supports an API.
obligations.conditional_on: Person meeting the 'covered provider' definition in Sec. 22757.1(b)

evidence.quote: A covered provider shall make available an AI detection tool at no cost to the user

obligations.summary: Collect user feedback on the efficacy of the AI detection tool and incorporate relevant feedback into efforts to improve the tool's efficacy.
obligations.conditional_on: Person meeting the 'covered provider' definition in Sec. 22757.1(b)

evidence.quote: A covered provider shall collect user feedback related to the efficacy of the covered provider’s AI detection tool

obligations.summary: Not collect or retain personal information from users of the AI detection tool (except contact information of users opting in to feedback contact, used only to evaluate and improve the tool); not retain submitted content longer than necessary; not retain personal provenance data from submitted content.
obligations.conditional_on: Person meeting the 'covered provider' definition in Sec. 22757.1(b)

evidence.quote: A covered provider shall not do any of the following:

obligations.summary: Offer the user the option to include a manifest disclosure identifying image, video or audio content as AI-generated, clear and conspicuous, and permanent or extraordinarily difficult to remove where technically feasible.
obligations.conditional_on: Person meeting the 'covered provider' definition in Sec. 22757.1(b)

evidence.quote: A covered provider shall offer the user the option to include a manifest disclosure

obligations.summary: Include a latent disclosure in AI-generated image, video or audio content, where technically feasible and reasonable, conveying the provider name, the GenAI system name and version, the time and date of creation or alteration, and a unique identifier (directly or via a link); the disclosure must be detectable by the AI detection tool, consistent with widely accepted industry standards, and permanent or extraordinarily difficult to remove where technically feasible.
obligations.conditional_on: Person meeting the 'covered provider' definition in Sec. 22757.1(b)

evidence.quote: A covered provider shall include a latent disclosure in AI-generated image, video, or audio content

obligations.summary: Where the provider licenses its GenAI system to a third party, require by contract that the licensee maintain the system's capability to include the latent disclosure; if the provider knows a licensee modified the system so that it can no longer include the disclosure, revoke the license within 96 hours of discovering the action.
obligations.conditional_on: Provider licenses its GenAI system to a third party (and, for revocation, knows of a modification by the licensee)

evidence.quote: the covered provider shall require by contract that the licensee maintain the system’s capability

obligations.summary: Third-party licensee of a GenAI system shall cease using the licensed system after the provider has revoked the license under Sec. 22757.3(c)(2).
obligations.conditional_on: License revoked by the covered provider under Sec. 22757.3(c)(2)

evidence.quote: A third-party licensee shall cease using a licensed GenAI system after the license for the system has been revoked
